questions.question: According to the policy, is the GitHub account created and linked to your first.last@noaa.gov email considered a personal account or a place to store your work-related organizational code?
options: It is an organizational account where work-related repositories can be stored directly under your username.
It is a personal account; all official work-related repositories must be created within the NOAA-GSL organization space.
It is a shared division account managed collectively by your Sponsor.
It automatically converts your personal workspace into a NOAA FISMA-accredited environment.
questions.correctAnswer: It is a personal account; all official work-related repositories must be created within the NOAA-GSL organization space.

questions.question: Are we required to license public code in our enterprise GitHub?
options: No, licensing is optional for scientific research software.
Yes, public code must require an approved license, such as Apache 2.0.
Only repositories with more than five active contributors require licensing.
No, public code is placed under default copyright with no license file needed.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, public code must require an approved license, such as Apache 2.0.

questions.question: Are we required to keep a README.md file associated with all repositories?
options: Yes, a README.md file must be applied to every single repository without exception.
No, a README.md is only required if a repository transitions to public access.
No, it is optional as long as the code includes inline documentation.
Only repositories transferred to non-NOAA enterprise accounts require a README.md.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, a README.md file must be applied to every single repository without exception.

questions.question: What authentication standard must all users enable on their GitHub account registered to their noaa.gov email?
options: SMS-only verification codes.
Single-sign-on (SSO) with biometric bypass.
Dual-factor (two-factor) authentication.
Security questions updated quarterly.

questions.question: What is the required timeframe for an Information Owner to address software vulnerabilities rated 'High' or greater in a public repository before public access is revoked?
options: Within 24 hours.
Within 3 days.
Within 14 business days.
During the next quarterly review cycle.

questions.question: How must a user's GitHub password relate to their NOAA account credentials (e.g., NEMS, ICAM)?
options: It must match your NOAA ICAM password for synchronization.
It must utilize a different password than that associated with any NOAA account.
It must be updated at the exact same time as your NOAA network credentials.
Passwords are not used; login is strictly handled through an external smart card.
questions.correctAnswer: It must utilize a different password than that associated with any NOAA account.

questions.question: Which email address must team members use when registering their GitHub account for NOAA-GSL access?
options: Any personal email address (e.g., Gmail, Outlook).
A cooperative institute or university affiliate address.
Their official noaa.gov email address.
An anonymous alias address.

questions.question: Which types of sensitive data are Information Owners strictly required to keep out of repository content?
options: Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Business Identifiable Information (BII).
Proprietary code or information.
All of the above.

questions.question: Which of the following defines and constitutes the role of an Information Owner under the GSL policy?
options: The owner of a repository (or multiple repositories), often serving as a project's Principal Investigator.
An individual responsible for authorizing access, establishing access/release policies, and approving public pull requests.
The person responsible for ensuring code contains no proprietary data, PII, or BII, and that software vulnerabilities rated 'High' or greater are resolved within three days.
All of the above.

questions.question: Whose permission must a Team Member obtain before creating a new repository in NOAA-GSL?
options: The Information System Security Officer (ISSO).
Their Division Sponsor (Division Chief).
The Department of Commerce Social Media Lead.
Any General User within the organization.
